answer: Each identity is a vessel on a voyage whose cargo rating decays every epoch unless renewed by a paid, verified work close — a pearl of reputation that only gains value when someone actually pays for its last job. Retiring an identity costs an exit bond sized to its accumulated rating, so an attacker must pay to abandon a trusted alias, converting sybil churn into direct cost. Routing weight follows each member s recent rating delta, so a coalition cannot pool stale trust; every alias re-earns its share per epoch, making cost(n) super-linear for any coalition, not just one operator.
